correctness.rationale: Under polynomial automorphism u=x,v=y+x^2,w=z, time is unchanged and the system is dot u=v^m, dot v=w, dot w=v^(2m)-1. Direct differentiation yields J^3=0. The planar Hamiltonian H=w^2/2+V_m(v), V_m=v-v^(2m+1)/(2m+1), has one center at v=-1 and saddle at v=1, so regular bounded ovals have turning points a(E)<-1<b(E)<1 and period T(E) and axial drift D(E) given by actual quadrature. Even m gives D>0. Odd m gives D<0 at E<=0 and center, while at saddle D=T+O(1)->+infinity; analyticity and nonzero endpoint signs give finitely many zeros of D in compact interior, hence a positive finite number of periodic cylinders. Nonzero drift ovals, planar equilibria and saddle-asymptotic branches have unbounded u, exhausting bounded forward trajectories. Quadratic saddle expansion gives coefficient 1/sqrt(2m) in log(1/(E_+-E)); subtracting T makes integrable v^m-1 cancellation. Independent quadratures for m=2..5 confirmed expected signs including near saddle; finite tests do not establish all-degree claims.

value.rationale: A motivated higher-monomial answer to the exact research question of periodic-surface multiplicity: all even degrees have no compact recurrence, each odd degree has finite nonzero families of physically isochronous periodic cylinders accounting for all bounded orbits. Explicit sharp separatrix drift/time behavior is nontrivial additional dynamical structure.

limitations: Only continuous real flow monomial degrees m>=2, not general defining polynomials, no exact odd cylinder count and no isolated/hyperbolic cycles.
